oneLiner: Retrofit autonomy for existing aircraft: a $105M-ceiling USSOCOM C-130J program, USAF KC-135 flight testing, and a first-of-its-kind NZ/FAA certification path -- trading ~75% below its March 2026 SPAC debut with ~$183M cash and a $32M revenue promise its $1M quarters have not yet met.
thesis: The certification lead is real and rare. Merlin completed SOI 1 and SOI 2 with the Civil Aviation Authority of New Zealand working in partnership with the FAA, and on Aug 6, 2026 announced SOI 3 for the Flight Control Computer and Automated Communication System, plus an agreed approach to certifying AI/ML natural-language components -- a first for the category.

Defense anchors the model while civil matures. The prime IDIQ with USSOCOM for C-130J autonomy carries a $105M ceiling, and the critical design review was completed Jun 4, 2026, moving the program into aircraft integration. KC-135 automation work with the USAF (agreement Feb 2024, flight testing with partner SNC since 2025) extends the tanker-fleet opportunity.

Aircraft-agnostic software is the scaling story. Merlin executed its first fully automated fixed-wing takeoffs on Apr 11 and Apr 21, 2026 (one in the US, one in New Zealand) and demonstrated an autonomous landing at EAA AirVenture Oshkosh on Jul 20, 2026; the Condor product family (announced May 14, 2026) extends Merlin Pilot to large multi-crew cargo and military aircraft.

The SPAC hangover is the price. Merlin listed Mar 17, 2026 via Inflection Point Acquisition Corp. IV at a ~$800M valuation with ~$200M of fresh capital; the stock has fallen from a $17 high to $4.16 (Aug 12), and targets were cut through July (Roth $15 to $10, TD Cowen $11 to $8) even as all four analysts stay at Buy.

Funding is adequate near term. Cash was ~$183M with no debt after an $80M PIPE closed May 1, 2026, against a $23.3M adjusted EBITDA loss in Q1 -- roughly seven quarters of runway at the current burn rate.

latestProse: Q1 2026 (reported May 14) was Merlin's first print as a public company and mostly accounting noise: the $(90.4)M GAAP loss reflects $87.8M of non-cash fair-value charges on convertible notes settled in the SPAC merger, against a $26.6M warrant gain. The operating reality is a $1.0M revenue quarter, a $(23.3)M adjusted EBITDA loss, and $28.8M of opex split evenly between R&D and G&A. Cash more than doubled to $122.8M and reached ~$183M after the May 1 PIPE, debt-free. Alongside earnings, Merlin launched Condor for large multi-crew aircraft and disclosed a non-binding MOU with freighter lessor World Star Aviation. The disclosure that matters most: revenue grew just 15% YoY to $1.0M -- the gap between that run-rate and the ~$32M 2026 projection in SPAC materials is the entire bear case.
guidanceProse: Merlin has issued no formal quarterly guidance; the IPO deck projected ~$32M of 2026 revenue, and Q2 results land today (Aug 13, after close) as the first real test of that arc. Funding is solid near term: ~$183M of cash, no debt, and roughly $23M per quarter of adjusted EBITDA burn imply about seven quarters of runway before new capital is needed. The central debate is whether C-130J integration, KC-135 flight testing, and SOI 3 certification progress convert into contracted revenue fast enough to justify a ~$400M market cap -- or whether Merlin is a well-funded R&D lab whose commercialization stays perpetually two years away. Sell-side remains Buy-rated but has cut targets steadily since May.
segments: Defense: USSOCOM C-130J autonomy prime IDIQ ($105M ceiling; CDR complete Jun 2026, now in aircraft integration), USAF KC-135 automation flight testing with SNC, and UAE opportunity scoping via the Remah International Group teaming agreement (Apr 23, 2026).

Civil: Merlin Pilot certification through NZ CAA with FAA coordination (SOI 3 achieved Aug 2026), targeting the first certified fully automated takeoff-to-touchdown fixed-wing flight; Condor for large cargo aircraft with a non-binding World Star Aviation MOU.
Essentially all reported revenue today is program and development work, not product sales.
competitive: Reliable Robotics is the closest comparable: Cessna Caravan continuous-autopilot STC path with the FAA plus its own USAF work -- arguably ahead on the US civil certification route, though still private.
Joby (JOBY) absorbed Xwing's autonomy division in 2024 and pairs a similar superpilot ambition with a multi-billion-dollar balance sheet spanning air taxis and defense.
Shield AI's Hivemind owns the combat-autonomy narrative at multi-billion private valuations, but targets uncrewed tactical jets rather than retrofit cargo and tanker autonomy.
Primes and incumbents bound the space: Lockheed/Sikorsky MATRIX, Airbus autonomy programs, and Garmin Autoland at the low end.

Versus platform peers Kratos (KTOS) and AeroVironment (AVAV), Merlin sells certified software retrofits for existing airframes rather than new unmanned aircraft -- a smaller market today, but capital-light if certification lands first.
moat: The certification archive is the intended moat: SOI 3 with the NZ CAA and an agreed pathway for certifying AI/ML-based components genuinely leads most rivals, and regulators move slowly for followers too. But nothing is certified yet, revenue runs ~$1M a quarter, the World Star and Remah agreements are non-binding, and a defense IDIQ ceiling is not backlog. Until a certified product ships or task orders convert, the moat is a well-documented head start, not a business.
risks: Commercialization gap: $1.0M Q1 revenue against ~$32M projected for 2026 in SPAC materials; guidance credibility is already impaired before the first full-year print.

Certification risk: SOI 3 covers two components; full takeoff-to-touchdown certification, FAA validation of the NZ path, and operational approvals for AI/ML systems remain unproven ground for any regulator.
Defense concentration and IDIQ optics: the $105M C-130J ceiling is a maximum, not contracted revenue; USSOCOM priorities, budgets, and timelines can shift.
Burn: ~$23M/quarter of adjusted EBITDA loss points to a funding wall around 2028 absent revenue inflection; the $80M PIPE arrived barely six weeks after listing.
Competition from better-funded players: Joby/Xwing, Shield AI, Reliable Robotics, and the primes can outspend Merlin many times over.
Post-SPAC technicals: the stock has traversed $17.00 to $3.27 in five months; lockup expiries and warrant overhang can cap rallies and amplify drawdowns.
catalysts: Q2 2026 results and first public-company outlook -- today, Aug 13, 2026, after market close.
First certified fully automated takeoff-to-touchdown fixed-wing flight with the NZ CAA (company target; watch H2 2026 into 2027).
C-130J aircraft-integration milestones and potential USSOCOM task orders through 2026-27.
KC-135 flight-test campaign progress with USAF/SNC and any movement toward a program of record in the FY2027-28 budget cycle.
Condor commercialization: converting the World Star Aviation MOU to a definitive agreement; outcomes from the UAE (Remah) teaming.
pricedIn: At $4.16 (Aug 12 close) on ~96.5M shares, market cap is ~$402M; net of ~$183M cash, enterprise value is ~$219M against $7.7M of TTM revenue -- nominally ~28x sales, but the market is pricing programs, not revenue. The stock has lost ~75% from its $17 March 2026 high, so SPAC froth is largely wrung out; four analysts average a $9.75 target. What is priced in: continued defense execution and eventual certification, with little near-term revenue. The debate is whether SOI 3 and the C-130J CDR were the last cheap milestones before revenue inflects in 2027, or whether certifying retrofit autonomy is a 2030s story that the 2026 cash pile cannot reach without heavy further dilution.

scenarios.bear: Q2 (Aug 13) shows another ~$1M revenue quarter with burn near $25M, and the $32M 2026 projection is quietly abandoned. Certification grinds -- flight-test evidence for AI/ML components takes years -- while USSOCOM task orders stay small and Condor remains an MOU. By late 2027 cash is under $60M, forcing a dilutive raise at depressed prices. The stock breaks its $3.27 low and settles toward cash value, roughly $2-3, as the market reclassifies Merlin as a funded lab rather than a product company.
scenarios.base: Defense revenue ramps as C-130J integration converts to billable task orders and KC-135 testing advances; 2026 revenue lands well below the $32M projection (perhaps $12-18M) but roughly doubles into 2027. The first certified automated flight arrives within about a year, validating the NZ CAA path. Burn moderates as programs bill. The stock ranges $4-8, re-rating on each contract or certification headline, with the 2028 funding question deferred rather than answered.
scenarios.bull: Certification lands: a certified takeoff-to-touchdown automated flight in late 2026 or 2027 makes Merlin the civil fixed-wing autonomy first mover, pulling Condor commitments from cargo operators and lessors. USSOCOM spends toward the full $105M ceiling and a KC-135 program of record emerges from the 2027 budget. Revenue exceeds $50M in 2027 on defense margins, and strategic interest from primes puts a floor under the story. The stock revisits $10-15 -- analyst-target territory -- without needing SPAC-era froth.

valPresets.note: Revenue mode because GAAP earnings are distorted by SPAC fair-value marks (Q1 GAAP loss $90.4M vs $23.3M adjusted EBITDA loss) and FCF is deeply negative. TTM revenue (~$7.7M) is a tiny, lumpy program-revenue base, so implied CAGRs look extreme -- read them as the growth defense task orders plus certified-product sales would need to justify the price, not as forecasts.
